live_web_research.page_text: [2610.11415] Refinement as a Service: Algorithmic Predictor Refinement Skip to main content Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search --> Computer Science > Computer Science and Game Theory arXiv:2610.11415 (cs) [Submitted on 8 Oct 2026] Title: Refinement as a Service: Algorithmic Predictor Refinement Authors: Wei Tang , Hanrui Zhang View a PDF of the paper titled Refinement as a Service: Algorithmic Predictor Refinement, by Wei Tang and 1 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Prediction aggregation aims to combine information from multiple predictors into a more informative one. We study this question in the setting of calibrated predictors, where each prediction must equal the conditional expectation of the quantity being predicted given the predictor's signal. Given several calibrated input predictors and the feature distribution, but not the underlying Bayes probabilities, we ask when one can construct refined calibrated predictors that preserve the information in the original predictors and cannot be further refined using the available information. We formulate calibrated predictors as signaling schemes and define refinement through feature-independent garblings: a predictor refines another if its signal can simulate the other's signal. Constructibility is characterized through observable linear information: each signal corresponds to a vector over the feature space, and a new signal is constructible exactly when its vector lies in the linear span of the input signal vectors. Under this formulation, we establish a sharp algorithmic picture. For deterministic output predictors, bilateral refinement admits a polynomial-time algorithm based on a bipartite graph between the two input signal partitions, while refinement with an arbitrary number of input predictors is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard. In contrast, when randomized output predictors are allowed, we give a polynomial-time algorithm for any number of input predictors by decomposing constructible signal vectors into extreme rays of the associated polyhedral cone. article.body:
‘Refinement as a Service’ proposes algorithms for combining calibrated predictors—not a documented software service

The paper studies how to construct a more informative calibrated predictor from existing predictors and a feature distribution, without access to the underlying Bayes probabilities. For randomized output predictors, it gives a polynomial-time algorithm for any number of inputs. With deterministic outputs, bilateral refinement has a polynomial-time algorithm, while refinement using an arbitrary number of inputs is NP-hard.

The paper specifies no customer group, software interface or product access. Its contribution is a theoretical algorithmic result, not evidence of a shipped capability; “as a Service” is part of the title, not a service launch. The paper is on arXiv and is listed as accepted by NeurIPS 2026; product availability not specified.
